3.0.s.en: 1. Between the fates of the wise righteous and the foolish wicked

3.0.0.en: 1 But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. 2 In the opinion of the foolish they died, and their departure was reckoned as misery, 3 and their going from us as destruction; but they are in peace. 4 And though in the sight of men they were punished, their hope is full of immortality. 5 And after a little chastening they have a great reward, for God tested them and found them worthy of himself. 6 As gold in the crucible he refined them, and received them as a burnt offering. 7 In the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run like sparks among the stubble. 8 They shall judge the nations and have dominion over the peoples, and their Lord shall reign for ever. 9 Those who trust in him shall understand the truth, and the faithful in love shall abide with him, for grace and mercy are to his chosen ones. 10 But the hypocrites shall receive the punishment that befits their counsels, since they despised the righteous and turned away from the Lord, 11 for he who despises wisdom and instruction is unhappy. Their hope is vain, their labours are without fruit, and their works are of no profit. 12 Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked, 13 and their offspring is cursed.

3.0.1.en: As for the souls of the righteous, they are in the hand of God, and no torment touches them. [1]

3.0.2.en: If the wicked go after death to eternal torment, the souls of the righteous are touched by no torment or harm; rather they settle and rest in the hand of God, enjoying perfect peace and receiving immortality.

3.0.3.en: The souls of believers in the Old Testament went down to Hades as a place of waiting, because redemption had not yet been accomplished; but they were not troubled, rather in true peace they awaited the coming of the Savior to break the bars of Hades and to lead them to Paradise with the thief on the right. But after the redemption, now the souls of the righteous pass, after leaving the body, to Paradise, where there is settledness and rest and the enjoyment of glories until the great day of the Lord, when the whole holy Church enters into the eternal Kingdom in heaven.

3.0.4.en: By saying that the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, the wise man declares not only that no torment touches them and that they find rest and settledness, but that they are the object of God's esteem and care; He keeps them in His hand as very precious in His eyes.

3.0.5.en: "They are in the hand of God" (Wis 3:1) means that they are under His protection, as it is said in Deuteronomy, "all thy saints are in thy hand" (Deut 33:3), and in Isaiah concerning Zion: "Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD" (Isa 62:3).

3.0.6.en: * For God finds the souls of the righteous (Jer 51:35), because the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God (Wis 3:1), but those souls of the wicked are counted as nothing.

3.0.7.en: Origen * The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God; here they bear the cross with Him, and they are in His hand also after their departure from the world, when their souls have rested from sufferings, the battles of the devil have ceased, and they have come to be in the Paradise of delight.

3.0.8.en: * The two lives cannot be separated; for in the midst of the spiritual battles we face in this life, God's care shines upon us, and He reveals His surpassing love and His arrangement for our eternal glories.

3.0.9.en: So we live here defying pain and sickness, and even the devil with all his hosts, and death, whatever its means. We live in a spirit of strength, not failure, and in a spirit of hope, not despair.

3.0.10.en: * The toil of all the long years of this present life disappears when we look to the eternity of the glory to come, and all our sorrows will vanish by thinking of the great blessing, and become like vapor that fades away as though it had never been; they are like lightning that vanishes the moment it appears.

3.0.11.en: St. John Cassian * We do not fear poverty or sickness or any such affliction, for we know that we are on our way to a better life, which is impregnable against death and destruction, and free from all injustice.

3.0.12.en: St. John Chrysostom * I rejoice in my sufferings, that He may gladden me with His radiance.

3.0.13.en: Since I bear His marks in my members (Gal 6:17), I rejoice because what I have endured abides in me.

3.0.14.en: * You receive the world of light in place of a bitter pain that you bear for His sake for one day.

3.0.15.en: If you endure hunger a little for the sake of His love, your desire to see His face is then kindled.

3.0.16.en: If darkness appears on your face from works done for His sake, He will adorn you with His glory for an endless eternity.

3.0.17.en: If you strip yourself of what is yours, He will clothe you with His light, and will hide from you what is yours.

3.0.18.en: If you leave what you possess, you will possess it in yourself eternally.

3.1.0.en: In the eyes of the foolish it seems that they have died, and their departure was reckoned as misery, [2]

3.1.1.en: The wicked are accustomed to look upon the end of the righteous as a punishment; this view differs from God's plan concerning reward and recompense, and it also corrupts the aspiration toward the holy life.

3.1.2.en: The wicked see in the departure of the righteous a catastrophe for them, because they did not enjoy temporal life, and there is no other world for them to enjoy. But the truth is that they come to be with God in peace. The righteous seem to have died, but in truth they are alive with God.

3.1.3.en: But the righteous look forward with joy to their departure from this world, that they may see the Lord face to face and feel in truth that they are in the hand of God; for even now, in their striving and amid sufferings, they feel the sweetness of the pledge of the heavenly life. Origen sees that the Holy Bible is in its essence the journey of the human soul from the world to the divine embrace. Thus, amid the striving, they perceive the surpassing touches of God's hand.

3.1.4.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus looked to his sister, older than he, St. Gorgonia, as a living model of the Christian, and he was greatly affected by her, for he was enamored of her godliness and piety. He explained how she prepared for death without fear, but rather longed for it:

3.1.5.en: * Gorgonia's homeland was the Jerusalem above (Heb 12:22, 23)... in which Christ dwells, and with Him share the assembly and the Church of the firstborn who are written in heaven...

3.1.6.en: * All that she was able to wrest from the ruler of this world she deposited in faithful places. She left nothing behind her except her body. She departed from everything for the sake of the heavenly hope. The only wealth she left to her children is the imitation of her example, and that they may enjoy what she deserved.

3.1.7.en: * Here I speak of her death and what distinguished her at that time, so that I may do her justice... She longed greatly for the time of her dissolution, for she knew Him who had called her, and preferred to be with Christ more than anything else on earth (Phil 1:23).

3.1.8.en: This saint longed to be freed from the bonds of the body and to escape from the mire of this world in which we live. And the more surpassing thing is that she tasted the beauty of her Beloved, Christ, since she was constantly contemplating Him.

3.1.9.en: She knew beforehand the hour of her departure from this world, which doubled her joy. And it seems that God made it known to her so that she might prepare and not be troubled then.

3.1.10.en: She spent all her life being washed from sin and striving to attain perfection. She received the gift of continual renewal by the Holy Spirit and became established in Him according to the merit of her former life..

3.1.11.en: She did not neglect to intercede for her husband also, that he might attain perfection, and God answered her petition, for she wished that everything connected with her should be in the state of perfection that God desires of us, so that nothing on her part would be lacking before Christ. And when the end came she gave her testament to her husband, her children and her friends, as is expected of such a saint who loved all.

3.1.12.en: Her last day on earth was a solemn day of festival, and we do not say that she died full of the days of the sons of men, for this was not her desire, since she knew that those days which are according to the flesh are evil, and are nothing but dust and mirage. Rather she was full of the days of God.. And so she was set free; or rather it is better to say that she was taken to her God, or escaped, or changed her dwelling, or quickly surrendered her deposit.

3.1.13.en: At the time of her repose a solemn silence prevailed, as though her death were a religious ceremony.

3.1.14.en: Her body lay as if in a state of paralysis after the soul had left it, and it became motionless.

3.1.15.en: But her spiritual father, who was watching her closely during this wonderful scene, sensed her murmuring and listened secretly, and behold, he heard her reciting the words of the psalmist: "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep" (Ps 4:8). Blessed is he who falls asleep with these words on his lips.

3.1.16.en: Thus you sang, O beautiful among women, and the song became reality. And you entered into the sweet peace after the pain, and you fell asleep as befits a woman beloved of God, who lived and reposed amid words of goodness.

3.1.17.en: How precious is your portion! It surpasses what the eye sees in the midst of a multitude of angels and heavenly powers; it is full of splendor, purity and perfection!

3.1.18.en: Surpassing all this is her seeing of the Holy Trinity, which is no longer far from the perception and sense that were formerly limited under the captivity of the body.

3.1.19.en: I hope that your spirit will accept this praise from me, as I did for my brother Caesarius. For I took care to pronounce praise for my brothers.

3.2.0.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus And their leaving us to be total destruction, but they are in peace. [3]

3.2.1.en: Some ask: will the souls of the righteous be joined with the souls of the wicked in one place, but the former full of peace and the latter full of bitterness and distress, or will each party be separated in a place independent of the other?

3.2.2.en: What we know is that the Lord Christ, by His descent into Hades, broke with His cross the bars of the abyss, and carried those who had died in hope as spoils with which He entered Paradise, where they enjoy surpassing glories. But on the great day of the Lord a general judgment takes place, and the glory of the righteous increases as they depart with their Bridegroom on the clouds as one glorious bride, enjoying entrance into the bosom of the Father.

3.2.3.en: * O wonder that truly surpasses nature! Astonishing events!

3.2.4.en: Death, formerly abhorred and condemned, is now surrounded by praises and considered blessed! After it used to bring mourning, grief, tears and gloomy sorrow, behold, it has appeared as a cause of joy, and a place for festal celebration!

3.2.5.en: For all the servants of God their death is proclaimed as joy! For the end of their life alone gives them the assurance that they have been accepted by God. Therefore he pronounced their death blessed, because it seals their perfection and shows their blessedness?, where the firmness of virtue prevails over them, as the inspired word says: "Judge none blessed before his death" (Sir 11:28).

3.2.6.en: We do not apply this saying to you (O Mary), because your blessedness does not come from death, and your death did not complete your perfection... Not at your death, but from this very conception you are called blessed by all generations. No, death was never what made you blessed, but you cast down death, scattered its gloom and showed that it is joy (in Christ whom you bore).

3.2.7.en: * Now let the heavens rejoice and let the angels clap!

3.2.8.en: Now let the earth be glad (Ps 96:11; 97:1), and let men leap for joy!

3.2.9.en: Let the air resound with songs of gladness, and let the pitch-dark night with its gloomy darkness and its mourning cloak be cast away; nay, since it has shone, let it imitate the gleam of day, the flashes of light.

3.2.10.en: Behold, the living city of the Lord God of hosts has been lifted up on high, and kings come with an offering beyond estimation from the temple of the Lord, from renowned Zion (Ps 68:29), in the Jerusalem above, which is free, and is the mother of them (Gal 4:26). And those whom Christ appointed as rulers over all the earth, that is, the Apostles, escort the ever-virgin Mother of God.

3.2.11.en: * Today the living city has been restored from the earthly Jerusalem to the Jerusalem above (Gal 4:26; Rev 21:10)!

3.2.12.en: * This tomb, though more precious than the old tabernacle, has contained the living spiritual lampstand shining with divine light, and the life-bearing table that received not the showbread but the heavenly Bread, not material fire but the immaterial fire of divinity.

3.2.13.en: * Let Mary, who is the Church, take the tambourine in her hands, and sing the song proper to the feast. Let the spiritual daughters of Israel come out with timbrels and dancing (Ex 15:20), uttering cries of joy!

3.3.0.en: Father John of Damascus And since in the eyes of men they were punished, their hope was full of immortality. [4]

3.3.1.en: Their suffering of any kind while they are on earth appears to be a punishment from God, but in truth it is a fatherly discipline, or a test to prove their faith, which prepares them the more to enjoy the Kingdom of God.

3.3.2.en: The author often repeats that the righteous hope for immortality or eternity, and ask it of God (Wis 3:4; 4:1; 8:13); it is a free grace that God offers them. The righteous man dies in the hope of enjoying everlasting life, which is denied to the foolish, who hope for nothing after death.

3.3.3.en: Some think that the word "immortality" appears here for the first time in the Holy Bible.

3.3.4.en: * For the servants of God there is peace, freedom and quiet rest; for when we withdraw from the storms of this world we reach the harbor of our city and our eternal security; when this death is accomplished we attain immortality.

3.4.0.en: The Martyr St. Cyprian And after a little chastisement they shall have a great reward, for God tested them and found them worthy of Himself. [5]

3.4.1.en: The heavens are opened before the sufferers to stand before the throne of Almighty God, and to realize that the affairs of men do not proceed haphazardly, but by a wonderful divine providence, for God, the Ruler of all, cares for all that touches man's life. This is the secret of our consolation amid affliction. So they repeat the saying: "In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul" (Ps 94:19), "for as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ" (2 Cor 1:5).

3.4.2.en: * The way of God's commandments is narrow, but the heart of him who runs in it is broad and wide, for it is the dwelling of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit; he walks it running with an enlarged heart... But the way of the evils of the wicked is wide and their hearts are narrow, for there is no place for God in them.

3.4.3.en: Anthimus, Bishop of Jerusalem * The way that leads to life is narrow and distressed (Mt 7:14), but the heart that goes about in it with a good circuit, that is, in the way of God's commandments, is broad and wide with the divine Word, and it is holy and sees God.

3.4.4.en: And on the contrary, the way that is "wide and broad, that leadeth to destruction" (Mt 7:13). But the heart (that walks in it) is narrow, it does not accept to make in it a dwelling for the Father and the Son (Jn 14:23), but ignores God because of its foolishness. This man makes his heart narrow because of his hardness.

3.4.5.en: Let us also consider how Solomon teaches us to inscribe the divine words on the tablet of our heart (Prov 3:4; 7:3; 22:20), declaring that "Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets" (Prov 1:20). By "without" he does not mean to speak of streets but of hearts, that God may enlarge them.

3.5.0.en: Origen As gold in the furnace he tried them, and as a burnt offering he received them. [6]

3.5.1.en: The wise man does not deny the chastening of the righteous, but only for a time. For the purpose of suffering is not destruction but purification, to remove every trace of down so that the metal is purified. Thus this precious metal (man) comes to be in the image of the holy God. Even gold can be purified, but the purification requires the presence of a furnace or fire; sacrifices too are good, but they are burned with fire so as to be offered as a burnt offering.

3.5.2.en: Amid our sufferings God accepts our spiritual burnt offerings, if He kindles in our souls by His Holy Spirit the fire of divine love that inflames our hearts within us, which many waters cannot quench. He grants within us the power of the resurrection and its victory over suffering and death and its eternal joy.

3.5.3.en: * The loving God tested the virtue of the righteous (Abraham) for a period of thirty years. And when God saw that he had been purified like gold in the furnace (Wis 3:6) for a long period of time, the virtue of this righteous man was made more radiant and brilliant; the Scripture says: "And when Abraham was ninety and nine years old, God appeared to him again" (cf. Gen 17:1).

3.5.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * If he who is above you is good he will be refreshing to you, but if he is evil he will be a criminal against you; in the first case receive the refreshment with joy, and in temptation show yourself true. Be gold. Look at this world as a goldsmith's furnace: in a narrow place there are three things: gold, straw and fire. The fire is applied to the first two: the straw burns, and the gold is purified. One man yields to threats, and is led to the temple of idols. Alas! I mourn for the straw. I see the ashes. And another does not yield to threats or terrors, and is led before the judge and confesses firmly without bowing to the image of the statue. What does the flame do to him? Does it not refine the gold? Stand firm in the Lord, brethren, for He who called you has a greater power. Do not fear the threats of the wicked. Bear with your enemies, for in them you find those for whom you pray. Do not be terrified of them in any way whatever.

3.5.5.en: This is saving health. Come out from this fountain to this feast, drink here where you are satisfied, and not from the other feasts by which you become frenzied. Abide in the Lord. You are silver and you will be gold. This comparison is not mine, but from the Holy Scripture, for you have read and heard "As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering" (Wis 3:6). See what you are among the treasures of God. Be rich by your contact with God, not as though you were making Him rich, but become rich through Him. Let Him satisfy you. Do not admit anyone else into your hearts.

3.6.0.en: St. Augustine In the time of their visitation they shall shine, and like sparks among the straw they run. [7]

3.6.1.en: After death the wicked realize the reward of the righteous, whom God their heavenly Father glorifies. And the wicked are exposed, because they lived with these righteous on earth in the very same circumstances, and perhaps even received more good things than they, and yet they did not believe in God, nor walk by His Holy Spirit.

3.6.2.en: After departing from this world the righteous shine like brilliant stars, and enjoy the vision of God and the fellowship of heavenly glory.

3.6.3.en: When he speaks of the fires of purifying trials he sees in the righteous that they shine all the more through these fires, which do not burn them, but burn the stubble (straw) in them, amid the night of this world, for warmth and light. This was the experience of farmers at that time.

3.6.4.en: Moreover, on another side, the fire of trials turns the righteous into something like torches blazing with fire, so that the darkness of this world's night is turned into day. While the wicked suffer the destruction of darkness, the righteous enjoy joyful radiance.

3.6.5.en: And on a third side, since they become blazing torches among the wicked, they kindle them with fire, so that they perish as long as they are determined on their evils. This is what was said by the prophet Obadiah about the house of Jacob and the house of Joseph, how they destroy the house of Esau as with a blazing fire! "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the LORD hath spoken it" (Obad 18).

3.6.6.en: "Visitation" is a biblical expression that points to divine intervention; here it points to His intervention on the great Day of Judgment.

3.6.7.en: "They shall shine" is a wonderful image of victory.

3.6.8.en: * Light also is the splendor of heaven for those who are purified here, when the righteous shine forth like the sun (Mt 13:34), and God stands in their midst (Wis 3:7), the gods and kings judge and distinguish the ranks of the beatitude of heaven.

3.6.9.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * The loving, merciful God Himself released the body from its captivity and freed it from the bondage of destruction, the bitter, deadly bondage, and granted it immortality in eternity. Thereby He gave the human body the gift of holy eternity, and made it immortal, never to die.

3.6.10.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * Truly they will be glorified and enjoy angelic exaltation, yet they remain human. The Apostle Paul remains Paul and Mary is Mary.

3.6.11.en: * If the promise to us is that we shall be like the angels, and there are not among the angels two distinct sexes, then we shall be without sexual distinction like the angels. In any case, when we rise from the dead we bear the sex that we have, but we do not exercise the function of sex.

3.6.12.en: St. Jerome * When every bodily desire is removed and there is no place in them for fleshly pleasures, they resemble the angels, rendering spiritual immaterial service, so that they become like holy spirits, and at the same time are counted worthy of a glory which the angels enjoy.

3.6.13.en: St. Cyril the Great * This was written especially, how Paul says plainly, "For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality (1 Cor 15:53).

3.6.14.en: So this body will rise and put on incorruption and take a new form. And as iron is mingled with fire and becomes fire, or rather as the Lord who raises us knows, this body will rise but will not remain as it is now.

3.6.15.en: It is an eternal body. It needs no nourishment for its life as it does now, nor steps for its ascent, for it will be spiritual. It is a wonder of which we are not worthy to speak. For it is said in the Gospel of St. Matthew the Evangelist, "Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father" (Mt 13:43), "and as the moon - and as the brightness of the firmament (Dan 12:3).

3.6.16.en: So God, who knows the unbelief of men, gave tiny worms to emit from their bodies rays of light, so that from what we see we may believe what we expect.

3.6.17.en: For God who gives the part is able to give the whole also.

3.6.18.en: And He who made the worm shine with light will rather make the pure man shine!

3.6.19.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * In eternal life all are fed with the food of righteousness and the drink of wisdom, and all are wrapped in immortality, and live in their eternal home, and eternity itself is the health of all, and their peace and their happiness, where there is no strife, no sickness, no death.

3.7.0.en: St. Augustine They shall judge the nations and have dominion over the peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them for ever. [8]

3.7.1.en: Salvation in the mind of many of the Jews is their enjoyment, as a nation, of dominion over the whole world, so that they have lordship over the peoples in the Messianic age. They understood a statement like this one before us in the literal sense, supposing that they are righteous who will dominate all the wicked peoples, and compel them to become Jews.

3.7.2.en: Those who realize that their souls are in the hand of God [1] enjoy a spirit of strength, and feel that they are kings in the hand of the King of kings. Their lives shine with the reflection of God's glory upon them, so they become judges of the nations that refuse to enjoy God's company, and have dominion over the peoples that think they have authority over the righteous.

3.7.3.en: Moreover we may say that, being in the hand of God, we judge the nations within us and have dominion over the peoples within us. We bear authority over our thoughts, our feelings and our emotions. With authority we tell evil thoughts to go out and they go out, and every uncleanness to depart from us and it flees from us. And with authority we call for holy emotions and feelings full of love and righteousness, and they hearken to us.

3.7.4.en: * He did not come with the aim of bringing about the unbelief of the Jews... The divine arrangement was wonderful... for He used the sin of the Jews to call the Gentiles to the Kingdom of God through Christ, though they were strangers from the covenants of promise (Eph 2:12).

3.7.5.en: We Christians say that the Jews, despite their former enjoyment of God's favor, since they were more beloved by Him than others, yet this divine arrangement and grace have been transferred to us, when Jesus transferred the authority that worked among the Jews to the believers from the Gentiles.

3.8.0.en: Origen Those who trust in Him shall understand the truth, and the faithful in love shall dwell with Him, for grace and mercy are to His saints, and He tends His chosen ones. [9]

3.8.1.en: Since we realize that our souls are in the hand of God, we will seek nothing less than to know the divine truth.

3.8.2.en: "Truth" here refers to the true knowledge of God, and the enjoyment of heavenly wisdom.

3.8.3.en: And as we know the divine "truth" we practice love as a gift of His Holy Spirit in us. We walk faithfully and are made worthy to dwell with God, and we experience His grace and mercy.

3.8.4.en: * Through the generosity of the One who gives us the greatest of all gifts, His very life.

3.8.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * (Since He became man) we are now able to possess Him, possess Him thus in greatness and in His very nature (as to His humanity) which He had, if we prepare for Him a fitting place in our souls.

3.8.6.en: * Christ, who is every virtue, comes and speaks on the basis that the Kingdom of God is within His disciples and is not here and there.

3.9.0.en: Origen But the wicked shall receive the punishment suited to their thoughts, for they are those who did not regard the righteous, and forgot the Lord. [10]

3.9.1.en: In contrast to the great end of the righteous we see the bitter end of the wicked, who receive eternal punishment for their complete insistence on not accepting the work of God's grace, their resistance to the divine truth, and their rejection of the divine commandment. The former come forward with the fruit of love in humility, and the latter offer the fruit of hatred, injustice and selfishness and their complete rejection of God's wisdom, and their walking in the error of evil. St. Anthony the Great says in the Sixth Letter that demons have no bodies, but when we accept their thoughts within us we respond to them, and so become like bodies for them. In this way the enemy of good turns our depths into hell, and our conduct bears the nature of the enemy of good.

3.9.2.en: * You should know that we become bodies for them (the demons) when our souls accept their dark evil thoughts, and when they become visible through our body in which we dwell.

3.9.3.en: St. Anthony the Great St. John Chrysostom did not wish to speak of the location of Gehenna other than that it is "outside this world. But he spoke in some detail of its curses. In one of his homilies he says of it:

3.9.4.en: [It is a sea of fire, not a sea of the same kind with the dimensions we know here, but greater and fiercer, with waves of fire, strange terrifying fires. There is there a great abyss full of terrifying flame. One can see the fire coming out of it from every side like a ravenous beast...

3.9.5.en: There, none is able to resist, none is able to escape.

3.9.6.en: There the gentle face of Christ, the giver of peace, is not seen anywhere.

3.9.7.en: And as those condemned to work in the mines are violent men, who no longer see their families, but those who force them to labor, so it will be there, but not so simply, rather what is far worse. For here a man can present a petition to the emperor asking for mercy and the prisoner may be pardoned, but there this will not happen. They will not go out but remain, enduring inexpressible torments.]

3.9.8.en: Again he says that the fires there neither consume man nor give light but burn continually. For the risen, condemned bodies are changed to deathlessness, therefore they continue to suffer torments eternally.

3.9.9.en: In spite of all these torments, the chief torment of the condemned is their deprivation of the presence of the Lord and the fellowship of the saints in heaven.

3.9.10.en: The degrees of torments differ in hell, depending on the extent of a man's sins, but all fall under them eternally.

3.9.11.en: He says: [It is impossible that the torments of Gehenna do not exist.]

3.9.12.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that these torments are not merely for the realization of divine justice, but were set to urge mankind to repent and abstain from sin.

3.9.13.en: [If God cares that we do not sin and that we enter into such troubles for our correction, it is clear that He punishes sinners and crowns the righteous.]

3.9.14.en: He says that He threatens with Gehenna so that no one may be cast into Gehenna.

3.9.15.en: What does he mean by saying: "the punishment suited to their thoughts"?

3.9.16.en: Perhaps he is answering here the questions of some: if God is love, how does He punish wicked people with the fire of eternal Gehenna? Where is God's infinite love for mankind? Does a man remain in eternal torment for sins or evils he committed for a period of time?

3.9.17.en: The answer to these questions is that God, who is all love, gave man the perfection of freedom, and this is the greatest gift; without it man loses the most important main trait that distinguishes him from the rest of earthly creatures. Through this freedom he is given the possibility of constant change between his accepting life with God eternally, or withdrawing from God finally. So whoever seriously chooses fellowship with God, God gives him the desire of his heart, and whoever insists on refusing fellowship with God, He does not compel him to it, but fulfills for him the desire of his heart, leaving him to receive what he has chosen.

3.9.19.en: If a father made every effort with his son that he should live seriously, but the son insisted on disobedience in recklessness and defiance, then when he reaches maturity with an abnormal personality, he cannot blame his father, since he wasted the opportunities to prepare himself to be mature.

3.9.20.en: If advice were offered to a boy to be earnest in his study with many warnings, and he insisted on laziness and play, then when he reaches the age for study he finds himself unfit for a decent profession, the opportunities of study having been lost to him, and ignorance having become his constant companion!

3.9.21.en: If a mother warned her son time and again not to touch anything hot, and in moments when she left him he tried to grasp a piece of glowing iron, he cannot blame his mother because the fire struck him, and he may remain for years treating what he did in seconds! And perhaps the marks of it remain in his hand all the days of his life!

3.9.22.en: Here too the blame falls only on the wicked themselves, for they taste eternally what they chose for themselves. And what did they choose?

3.10.1.en: Three grave matters utterly destroy the wicked. The first is that they "did not regard the righteous," that is, they found pleasure in practicing injustice against the righteous, and made every effort to be rid of him at any price. By this they deprive themselves of fellowship with the righteous and the saints, seeking another place in which there is no righteous or just man. Thus they chose Gehenna and not the Kingdom of God!

3.10.2.en: The second matter is that they "forgot the Lord"; that is, they gave Him the back and not the face; so how can they meet Him in His Kingdom, or how can they be happy to meet Him whom they reject with all their hearts?

3.10.3.en: And the third matter is their despising of wisdom and instruction, as we see in the following statement:

3.10.4.en: For he who despises wisdom and instruction is unhappy:

3.10.5.en: Their hope is vain, their labours are unprofitable, their labours are unfruitful, and their works are unprofitable. [11]

3.10.6.en: If wisdom is the enjoyment of the eternal wisdom of God and the possession of immortal righteousness, then whoever rejects wisdom, and does not accept God's plan for him, and murmurs against discipline, chooses misery for himself, and loses all hope, and all his labor becomes without profit or fruit!

3.10.7.en: The effect of despising wisdom and instruction does not stop at directing man's life here on earth, but extends to the eternal life, which is in its essence the acceptance of fellowship in glory with the eternal wisdom of God.

3.10.8.en: Whoever rejects wisdom here cannot bear it there; and whoever thinks that his happiness is in amusement while murmuring against the Lord's discipline of him here loses eternal happiness.

3.11.0.en: Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked, and their offspring cursed. [12]

3.11.1.en: "Foolishness" in the books of wisdom is bound up with evil; the fool equals the wicked. The wicked cleave to foolish or wicked women, who bear sons and daughters who walk as their parents.

3.11.2.en: If the righteous seeks wisdom as an eternal bride, is joined to her, and enjoys her sweetness, her beauty and her immortality, the wicked seeks ignorance as a companion for himself, and death becomes his comrade, united with him and becoming of his party.

3.11.3.en: The children of the righteous who are joined to wisdom are the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, goodness, meekness, temperance, etc. (Gal 3:23). But the children of the wicked who are joined to ignorance are hatred, bitterness, murmuring, confusion, pride and every vice.

3.12.0.en: 13 But blessed is the barren woman who is pure, who has not known the sinful bed, for she shall have her fruit in the visitation of souls. 14 And blessed is the eunuch whose hand has not engaged in sin, nor has his heart devised evil against the Lord; for he shall be given a lofty grace for his faithfulness, and a desirable portion in the temple of the Lord. 15 For the fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of prudence is firm. 16 But the children of adulterers shall not attain their full strength, and the offspring of the sinful bed shall perish.

3.12.1.en: But blessed is the barren one who is undefiled, who has not known a sinful bed, for she shall have fruit at the visitation of souls. [13]

3.12.2.en: Among the Jews the bearing of children was a sign of God's pleasure with a person, and barrenness a sign of a curse.

3.12.3.en: Every woman in the Old Testament hoped that the Messiah, the Savior, would come from her offspring, and if she was barren people counted her unworthy of the divine blessing. But the wise man, to whom the greatness of virginity had been revealed, preferred those who live without children according to the flesh, with the consecration of their hearts and energies to the love of God and His service on earth for the sake of the heavenly wedding, over marriage with the bearing of children.

3.12.4.en: What he says about the virgin maiden he repeats concerning the young man; the eunuch who cannot marry and beget sons, without breaking the commandment by the practice of evils, awaits the reward in heaven.

3.12.5.en: The spiritually virgin person is he who loves God with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his might, so that the world no longer has any trace in his depths, but his soul is prepared as a virgin bride who rests only in the bosom of her heavenly Bridegroom.

3.12.6.en: * The man who looks with a pure spiritual look through the illusions of this life, rising above its struggle, appreciating its triviality, withdrawing from it entirely by abstaining from marriage. This man comes to have no further fellowship with the evils of mankind, such as malice, envy, anger, hatred and everything of the sort; he is exempt from all this, and enjoys freedom and lives in peace. There is nothing to arouse his neighbor's envy, for he possesses of the debris of this life nothing around which the envy of others gathers.

3.12.7.en: He has risen by his own life above this world, and virtue has become his only precious possession. He will spend his days in quiet and peace unmixed with bitterness, because virtue is a wealth in whose ownership all share, each according to his ability, and it is available to all who thirst for it, unlike the ownership of land in this world, which men divide into parts. And whenever one adds a new piece of land to his share, another person's share of it is correspondingly diminished. One gains at the expense of his fellow's loss, and from here battles arise. One wants to obtain the lion's share, and thereby brings upon himself the hatred of others if he deceives them. But he who possesses virginity is never envied by anyone.. He who possesses the lion's share of it causes no harm to him who claims for himself a similar share. And as long as each of them can obtain this life, each can obtain of it whatever he wishes for himself. The wealth of virtues never runs dry.

3.12.8.en: * I consider that virginity is the scientific method in the science of heavenly life, which supplies man with the power to be united with spiritual natures.

3.12.9.en: * Virginity aims to create in the soul a complete forgetfulness of natural passions; it will prevent the process of continual descent to satisfy bodily desires. And once the soul is freed from such things, it does not hazard the undefiled heavenly delights by being ignorant of them and heedless of them, and it abstains from the habits that involve man in what the law of nature seems to some extent to concede.. It is the purity of heart that prevails in life that alone then captivates the soul.

3.12.10.en: The Martyr St. Cyprian And blessed is the eunuch whose hand has done no iniquity, and who has not thought evil thoughts against the Lord!

3.13.0.en: For he shall receive for his faithfulness a lofty gift, and a desirable portion in the temple of the Lord. [14]

3.13.1.en: After he spoke of the virginity of the maiden under the expression "the barren one who is undefiled," to declare that lasting spiritual fruit is not merely the begetting of children according to the flesh, but the begetting of sons in the Lord through the practical witness of the spiritual wedding between the human soul and God, now he speaks of the virginity of the young man under the expression "the eunuch whose hand has done no iniquity." And the Lord Christ presented to us a call to virginity by saying: For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother's womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it (Mt 19:12). The Lord Christ distinguishes between virginity that is from natural incapacity, and virginity from enslavement, such as a master compelling his slave to it, or some philosophers imposing it by force when they make some of those subject to them weak in sexual capacity for the practice of pagan worship. And the third is what the Book of Wisdom means, that is, virginity for the sake of the Kingdom of God, which a man chooses when he is called to it, able to practice it spiritually as well as bodily.

3.13.2.en: Virginity is not an end in itself, but a challenge to human nature through the surpassing grace of God, where the believer accepts to challenge the demands of the body, not as humiliation of it nor as defilement of marriage, God forbid! but a person practices it as a declaration of selling everything to acquire his fellowship with his heavenly Bridegroom at the highest level. He acquires the pearl of great price, and so consecrates all his thoughts to the glory of the Lord. The wise man says: "he shall receive for his faithfulness a lofty gift, and a desirable portion in the temple of the Lord" [14]. This is also what the prophet Isaiah affirmed in his songs for the first-born Church, and for every member who enjoys virginity of heart, mind and soul:

3.13.3.en: "Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear.

3.13.4.en: Break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD.

3.13.5.en: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations.

3.13.6.en: Spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes. For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left; and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited" (Isa 54:1-3).

3.13.7.en: "Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree. For thus saith the LORD unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my covenant;

3.13.8.en: Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off" (Isa 56:3-5).

3.13.9.en: In [(Isa 54:1), the Septuagint] it says "Cry out and rejoice, you who did not travail." And St. Cyril the Great and also Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrrhus, see that it was the custom of the midwife to ask the woman who finds difficulty in labor and is in severe pain to cry out, that this may help her in giving birth.

3.13.10.en: Here is a prophecy about the Church of the Gentiles, which was pagan without a bridegroom; when she received the Lord Christ as her Bridegroom she cries out in her struggle, but with a spirit of singing and joy, and so bears many holy children to the Lord.

3.13.11.en: So it is fitting for the virgin not to cease from striving with strong spiritual cries with great rejoicing, and so bear many children to the Lord, through his living practical witness.

3.13.12.en: * "Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree" (Isa 56:3). In this statement he urges the eunuchs to virtue, and crushes the arrogance of those who lean upon the multitude of children for the attainment of glory.

3.13.13.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrrhus * Riches (spiritual) were promised to the believers, and as it was said to us: [There was not one feeble person among their tribes] (Ps 105:37). And now it is said even to the eunuchs: "Do not say: Behold, I am a dry tree." For instead of sons and daughters you have a place in heaven. Now He pronounces the poor blessed... Now the weak is counted strong.

3.13.14.en: St. Jerome * Virginity is stronger than death, and this being is rightly called immortal, because it renders no service to a mortal world, and does not exhaust itself to become a means of mortal offspring. In such a body the agents of corruption and death, which entered into the first man, have ceased.

3.13.15.en: * Virginity is not a struggle that ends with the subjection of the body, but it expands in its scope until it includes everything in the soul. It is the state of the complete health of the soul so that the true Bridegroom may be its portion. It does not only keep away from all the uncleannesses of the body, but makes of this asceticism only the beginning of the process of its purification on the widest scale, so that it keeps itself safe from falling into any passion of the soul during its course.

3.14.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa For the fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of wisdom shall never fail. [15]

3.14.1.en: When the wise man compares what is enjoyed by the righteous, whose souls are in the hand of God, and the wicked who despise wisdom and resist truth and righteousness, who forget the Lord, he declares that the fruit of good labors is glorious, and that what the wise receive are genuine blessings that will not pass away, but become for him a crown of glory in heaven.
